Subject: POC traffic windowing & econ — clarifying asks and next steps

Hi Sam / Nina — great to hop on earlier. Short follow-up with the specific asks we need to scope a tight 2-week POC and give a firm ballpark on unit economics. Please reply with the items below (even approximate numbers are helpful):

- Expected monthly token volume band (low / typical / peak month)
- Typical request size: average prompt tokens, average generated tokens
- % of requests that will be streamed vs standard response
- Concurrency profile: baseline qps and spike qps (and typical duration of spikes)
- Any hard latency SLOs (p50/p90 target) and whether you prefer p50-sensitive or p90-sensitive configs
- Target $/1M tokens you’re budgeting for (we use this to size Dedicated vs Hosted recommendations)

What we’ll provide once we have the above: a two-week POC plan (traffic ingestion, sandbox routing, SLOs), a recommended concurrency and batching config, and a ballpark pricing sheet showing hosted vs dedicated with the assumed batching benefits. I attached a short one-pager with our baseline econ assumptions for similar customers.

Next steps suggested: if you can send the numbers by EOD Monday, we’ll turn around a POC plan and pricing the same day. Also helpful if you can share a small sample of traffic (schema is fine) or confirm an S3 share.

Thanks — happy to jump back on a quick sync if that’s easier.

—
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — good recap. Answers below (ballpark):

- Monthly token volumes: low ~120M, typical ~260M, peak month up to ~520M
- Typical request: prompt ~80 tokens, response ~220 tokens (we expect the average response length to shrink as we tune)
- Streaming: ~25% of requests will use partial streaming (progressive responses)
- Concurrency profile: baseline ~50 qps, short promotional spikes up to ~600 qps for 10–30 minutes, sustained spikes up to ~200 qps for 2–3 hours during business events
- Latency SLOs: target p50 < 200ms for interactive UI flows; p90 < 600ms acceptable for batch/long-running tasks. Our product team cares more about p50 for that main UI path.
- Budget target: we’re looking for ~$60 per 1M tokens as a target; room to flex to $45–75 depending on guarantees and POC outcomes.

I can provide an S3 sample of anonymized requests (schema only) — will have that to you by EOD Monday. Also attaching a sample traffic schema.

Sam

Thanks for the detailed numbers, Sam — this is exactly what we need. A few clarifications and the high-level econ and batching assumptions we’ll use to size options: 

Clarifications
- When you say "baseline 50 qps", is that sustained over 24 hours or concentrated in your primary US region daytime? (helps with autoscaling policies)
- For the 600 qps promo spikes, can you confirm whether those are primarily short-lived bursts (<30m) or a mix of 30–60m?

Redwood ballpark econ assumptions we’ll apply
- Continuous batching window: we typically configure a 40–80ms aggregation window for interactive workloads to capture micro-batches without adding perceptible latency. For your p50-sensitive flow we’d bias to 40–60ms.
- Effective batching benefit: with 25% streaming and expected reuse patterns (KV cache hit ~15–25%), we conservatively model a 15–25% unit-cost reduction from continuous batching + KV cache for your workload. The benefit increases when request size is small and when we can reuse prefixes across requests.
- Concurrency guidance: for low-latency UI flows, we recommend starting with 8–12 concurrent request slots per GPU pod and scale-to 48–64 slots per pod for background/throughput modes; we’ll tune during POC.
- Latency expectation: with the above config, we expect to meet p50 < 200ms in most cases; p90 will depend on tail behavior during the 600 qps bursts unless we add burst capacity or fallbacks to a faster, smaller model.

Preliminary pricing framing (very rough; will finalize after POC traffic capture)
- Hosted (no commit): list-rate equivalent for similar configs would be ~$80–90 / 1M tokens; with continuous batching benefits applied to your profile we can be in the ~$55–70 / 1M tokens range.
- Hosted (short POC commitment + volume discount): we can target $50–60 / 1M tokens for the first 3 months of the POC depending on measured batching gains.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity, 6–12 month): with committed volume your unit can approach $35–45 / 1M tokens after amortizing reserved costs and aggressive batching/caching.

Recommended next steps
1) Share the S3 sample (schema + a small slice of anonymized traffic) — we’ll run it through our simulator in 24 hours and return a tuned batching/concurrency config.
2) 2-week POC: we’ll instrument token-level cost reporting, latency SLOs, and an econ dashboard.
3) After the POC, we’ll present final pricing options (hosted vs dedicated) with measured $/1M tokens and recommended deployment modes.

I’ve attached a short 2-page econ summary; we’ll produce a detailed POC plan once we ingest the sample. Shall I go ahead and draft the POC statement of work and hit you with a short SOW + DocuSign link?

—
Jasmine Liu
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
